title: Sam Parr on insecurity as fuel, delegating to a CEO, and a boring daily routine
summary: Sam Parr tells Andrew Wilkinson how he went from a hot dog stand to The Hustle exit, MFM and Hampton. He covers why feeling inadequate drives ambition, why meeting successful founders removed his fear, hiring a CEO to run Hampton, and the narrow circle of trust and fixed routines he keeps.

principles.text: Admire peers instead of tearing them down; aim to build your own skyscraper next to theirs.
principles.quote: I don't want to crush your Tower it's like I want to have a skyscraper just as big because I want to feel adequate

principles.text: Successful people are as flawed and fearful as you, so don't let them intimidate you out of competing.
principles.quote: the people I admire are screw-ups and fearful just like I am and it felt like I used to have bad eyesight and once I met these people and got to intimately know them I put good eyeglasses on

principles.text: Hire a CEO to run daily operations while you focus on the few things where you add the most value, like marketing and spotting opportunities.
principles.quote: I'm like the marketing department because I've got the podcast and I've got my personality whatever you want to call my brand and that drives growth

principles.text: Delegating people problems is a big upside; you still work as much but only on high-value work.
principles.quote: I only focus on things that I actually add a significant amount of value towards

principles.text: Build a small, fully trusted inner circle and be guarded with everyone else.
principles.quote: it's important you just have this tight tribe

principles.text: Seek time freedom: work hard for a short period so you can spend your time how you want.
principles.quote: the best way to win is to have enough money that you could tell anyone to go [ __ ] themselves and I could spend my time how I want
